claim: The World Wide Web was invented by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN in 1989 using HTTP HTML and URLs to create a hypertext information system
Open source software allows anyone to inspect modify and distribute source code fostering collaborative development and innovation
Cloud computing delivers on-demand computing resources over the internet eliminating the need for local hardware management
Blockchain is a distributed ledger technology that records transactions across many computers so that records cannot be retroactively altered
The Internet of Things connects physical devices sensors and actuators to the internet enabling data collection and remote control
End-to-end encryption ensures that only the communicating users can read messages preventing interception by intermediaries including service providers
IPv6 provides approximately 340 undecillion addresses solving the address exhaustion problem of IPv4 which supports only 4.3 billion addresses
Solid state drives use flash memory with no moving parts providing faster read/write speeds and greater durability than traditional hard disk drives
Edge computing processes data near the source of data generation reducing latency and bandwidth usage compared to centralized cloud computing
Mesh networking enables devices to connect directly to each other without centralized infrastructure providing resilient communication in challenging environments
Digital twin technology creates virtual replicas of physical systems enabling simulation testing and optimization before making real-world changes
Zero-trust security architecture verifies every access request regardless of network location assuming no user or device is inherently trustworthy
Progressive Web Apps combine web accessibility with native app features including offline support push notifications and home screen installation
RSS and Atom feeds enable users to subscribe to content updates from websites without relying on proprietary platforms or algorithms
Tor routes internet traffic through multiple encrypted relays to protect user anonymity and circumvent censorship
IPFS is a peer-to-peer protocol that addresses content by its cryptographic hash enabling distributed and censorship-resistant file storage
WebAssembly enables near-native performance in web browsers by providing a portable binary instruction format for languages like Rust C and Go
Kubernetes orchestrates containerized applications across clusters of machines automating deployment scaling and management
RISC-V is an open instruction set architecture that enables anyone to design processors without licensing fees promoting hardware innovation
Differential privacy adds calibrated noise to data queries enabling useful statistical analysis while mathematically guaranteeing individual privacy
